what: What brings a Flow-flagged account (PUBLIC_ERROR_UNUSUAL_ACTIVITY) back to automated sends: every account packs takes on a day budget that starts at 10 (new, or back from a flag; 25 until 2026-10-22) and climbs while it stays unflagged, com none until its first flag; the marker's arms vary one thing each — 'time' (jihangarangan: one probe when the 48 h wall ends, 2026-10-17 05:00), 'hand-done' (egbogd, loiyehor: the owner's hand session 2026-10-15 evening, probe the same night, about 18 h after the flag; tronjhon from 2026-10-16), 'hand-first' (rawilimo, abel after flow-rest: walled until the owner closes his own Flow session in the automation profile), 'manual' (locomthebest; sergey from 2026-10-18: its hand Pro 4-packs passed while the identical automated request flagged on 2026-10-16, and its first automated send after the wall flagged again on 2026-10-18 16:24 with the hand session's launch flags: walled, owner by hand only), 'control' (com: no budget until its first flag). Hand probes pass and time probes flag: a hand session ends the wall; all four flag: the automated session itself is the cause (warm long-lived Chrome next)
evidence: per account: flagged_at / flag_strikes / saved_at / flow_takes in ~/.gemini-web/accounts/<a>.json, 'Flow flagged this account' reports in ~/.gemini-web/failures/, queued (with refs fingerprints and count), saved, failed (reason, flagged) and hand (owner sessions) rows in ~/.gemini-web/jobs.jsonl; baseline 2026-10-15: five accounts flagged at their 30th-36th image of a night, com clean at 97
surfaces: menubar Gemini account rows (the arm walls)
how_to_remove: Read the evidence per arm and ask the owner which change stays. Then delete every TEMP-FLOW-TRUST(gemini-web) block (share/gemini_web.py: trust, trust_arm, trust_hand_done and their call sites in cmd_login, cmd_accounts; the block in tests/test_flow_image.sh), delete ~/.gemini-web/flow-trust.json, set flow_day_takes in ~/.gemini-web/accounts/<a>.json to what the verdict says (or remove it), clear the arm walls the owner releases in ~/.gemini-web/walls.json, then this entry, and run tests/run-all $(tests/affected share/gemini_web.py).

what: The claude.ai Artifact tool stays ON (no enableArtifact key in ~/.claude/settings.json, shared by every claudeb profile) only so the pixel-forge chat can keep reading its claude.ai vote page until the local pages kit (docs/handoffs/2026-10-28-pages-plan.md) ships the compare module and pixel-forge votes through `page`; Egor turned artifacts off on 2026-10-28 and re-enabled them for this bridge alone («потом обязательно отключим»)
evidence: pixel-forge chat (claude-setup) voting through `page` instead of its artifact; `jq .enableArtifact ~/.claude/settings.json`
surfaces: the Artifact tool itself in every chat
how_to_remove: Once pixel-forge votes through `page`: set "enableArtifact": false in ~/.claude/settings.json (jq into a temp file, then write it back over the real file — every profile symlinks it), confirm `jq .enableArtifact ~/.claude/settings.json` prints false, then delete this entry and run tests/run-all $(tests/affected EXPERIMENTS.json).
